extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, and obituary writers seeking an overview of obituary conventions and practices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and conventions for producing newspaper-style obituaries, advance/prewritten obituaries, paid death notices and memorial advertisements, and editorial policies to avoid premature publication. Covers stylistic, procedural, and selection criteria used by news organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced account and deadpan style (avoid hagiography)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obituaries ought to be 'balanced accounts' written in a 'deadpan' style, and should not read like a hagiography. Although obituaries tend to focus on positive aspects of the subject's life, this is not always the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with even tone; include achievements and context without idolizing the subject. Avoid overt hero-worship while still recognizing accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local obituary eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: In local newspapers, an obituary may be published for any local resident upon death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local residency is often sufficient criteria for publication in community papers; level of detail may vary by outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necrology vs. obituary (scope and detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: A necrology is a register or list of deaths of people related to a particular organization, group or field and may contain the sparsest details or small obituaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use necrologies for concise record-keeping; they can be important historical sources but are distinct from fuller obituary articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death notice (paid advertisement) format and legal role
rubrics_metrics.description: A death notice (a type of paid advertisement) usually appears in the Births, Marriages and Deaths (BMD) section, omits most biographical details and may be a legally required public notice under some circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat death notices as classified/legal notices rather than biographical pieces; expect minimal personal history and formal phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorial advertisement authorship and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Memorial advertisements are usually written by family members or friends, perhaps with assistance from a funeral home, and are usually run as classified advertisements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and tone are controlled by submitters (family/friends); publications generally treat these as paid classified items rather than editorial obituaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance/prewritten obituaries for notable individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Many news organizations maintain prewritten (or preedited video) obituaries on file for notable individuals who are still living, in order to promptly publish detailed, authoritative, and lengthy obituaries upon their deaths. These are also known as 'advance' obituaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prewritten obituaries are updated periodically; they enable rapid, researched publication and often exist in large 'reservoirs' at major papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to assign advance obituaries
rubrics_metrics.description: An advance obituary is usually not written until the subject has reached old age, as the earlier a profile is written, the more additions and revisions it will likely require. 'As a general rule, when lives are long enough, accomplished enough and complex enough that we would just as soon not get caught short writing them on deadline, advances are assigned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign advances for long, accomplished, or complex lives; occasionally prepare advances earlier for those with serious health issues or chaotic lives; major figures may have drafts maintained and revised for years or decades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing notables for obituary material
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York Times often interviews notables specifically for their obituaries, a practice begun by Alden Whitman in 1966.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary interviews with the subject can improve accuracy and depth of advance obituaries; this practice supports authoritative, first-person detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection based on influence and themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some outlets (e.g., The Economist) publish obituaries that reflect on the subject's life and influence on world history; other outlets publish themed obituary anthologies (military, sports, entertainers, eccentrics, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and presentation can be curated by perceived historical influence or thematic grouping; editorial judgment shapes which subjects receive feature-length treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies and sourcing to prevent premature obituaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly all newspapers now have policies requiring that death notices come from a reliable source (such as a funeral home) to avoid premature obituaries and hoaxes. Premature obituaries may occur due to miscommunication or system errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require verification from reliable sources before publication; implement editorial checks to prevent accidental release of prewritten obituaries (e.g., CMS safeguards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational practices for maintaining and updating advance obituaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance obituaries are often drafted, then updated repeatedly over years; large papers keep extensive 'reservoirs' of advances and may continually revise them (examples include multi-decade work on prominent figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain version control and periodic review of advance obits; adapt content and presentation formats over time to match changes in technology and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation of layout and digital presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-known advance obituaries have had their visual layout and digital presentation substantially modified over time to match changes in print page size, slideshow and video formats, and Internet download speeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design obituary presentation to fit the medium (print vs. digital), updating layout and multimedia elements as platforms evolve to best serve readers.
